blogs.title: The MODY Miss: Why We're Overlooking Monogenic Diabetes in Young Adults
blogs.description: This post will explore the diagnostic challenges in identifying MODY, focusing on why up to 80-90% of cases are misdiagnosed as Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes. Using the case as a springboard, we'll discuss the clinical red flags that should prompt consideration of MODY: strong family history with autosomal dominant pattern, negative autoantibodies, preserved C-peptide, and absence of insulin resistance features. We'll also address limitations of current screening tools like the Exeter MODY probability calculator, which was derived from White European populations and may misclassify patients from other ethnic backgrounds.

blogs.title: De-Prescribing Insulin: When Genetic Results Change Everything
blogs.description: A practical look at how genetic confirmation enabled this patient to transition off insulin therapy entirely. This post will discuss the paradigm shift from initial empiric treatment (appropriate given the clinical presentation) to precision medicine-guided therapy. We'll examine the evidence supporting GLP-1 receptor agonists as effective alternatives to sulfonylureas in HNF1A-MODY, with the added benefit of lower hypoglycemia risk and weight management. The post will emphasize the clinical and quality-of-life implications of making the right diagnosis.

blogs.title: HNF1A-MODY: A Therapeutic Minefield — Why SGLT2 Inhibitors Could Be Dangerous
blogs.description: This post will focus on the specific pharmacotherapeutic considerations unique to HNF1A-MODY. While sulfonylureas have long been first-line, emerging evidence supports GLP-1 receptor agonists as safer alternatives. Crucially, we'll discuss the often-overlooked risk of SGLT2 inhibitors in this population: due to reduced SGLT2 expression from HNF1A mutations, these patients have an inherently low renal threshold for glucose. Adding pharmacologic SGLT2 inhibition may precipitate severe dehydration, volume depletion, and euglycemic DKA—a critical warning for clinicians who might reflexively prescribe these agents for 'young-onset Type 2 diabetes.'

blogs.title: Beyond Autoantibodies: The Role of C-Peptide in Diabetes Classification
blogs.description: An in-depth analysis of how C-peptide testing, including the glucagon stimulation test used in this case, helps differentiate diabetes etiology. We'll discuss the interpretation of stimulated vs. fasting C-peptide, the gray zones that create diagnostic uncertainty, and why preserved C-peptide doesn't always rule out Type 1 diabetes (especially early in its course). The post will provide practical guidance on when to order these tests, what thresholds to use, and how to integrate results with autoantibody testing and clinical context.

blogs.title: Novel Genetic Variants in MODY: A Clinician's Guide to Variant Interpretation
blogs.description: This post will demystify the process of interpreting genetic testing results for clinicians who aren't geneticists. Using the novel p.N270S HNF1A variant from this case as an example, we'll explain how pathogenicity is assessed using ACMG guidelines, what tools like AlphaMissense scores mean, and why the absence of a variant from ClinVar doesn't make it insignificant. We'll also discuss the practical implications of discovering novel variants for family screening and the importance of genetic counseling in monogenic diabetes.
